column1: # perl-suite-fails.tsv — the ROW-level fail baseline for tools/run-perl-suite.pl
# answer to baselines/fail-baseline.tsv: until this file existed the 273 DIFF
# files were blessed as COUNTS only, so #964's failing row sat inside op/sub.t's
# "12 not ok" for months with nothing naming it.
# s492b (2026-09-21, Opus) -- FIVE rows removed BY EDIT, each because this batch
#   made it pass, each A/B verified `--jobs 1` against a 5ce155cb extraction:
#     io/pipe.t           child reaped if piped program cannot be...  #2006(a)
#     op/goto_xs.t        [perl #35878] croak in XS after goto...     #2004 (die flattens)
#   re/pat.t is the SIXTH, and its rows were re-spelled with `--bless-fails` for
#   THAT FILE ALONE (527 -> 525 keys, no other file touched) rather than edited:
#   its 12 real gains come from t/re/pat.t:45, where the row DESCRIPTION is itself
#   built by the `sprintf` #2004 fixed -- on a 5ce155cb extraction row 1 reads
#   `$0 = ` and here it reads perl's own `$1 = A`, so 80 old keys no longer
#   exist and 82 new ones appeared while the same tests kept failing.  Editing by
#   key would have been a guess: that file exceeds the 500-row log cap (its
#   baseline is PARTIAL) and its unnamed rowkeys redraw per run (#1965).  The
#   file-level row in baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv carries the cause too.
# One line per DIVERGING TAP row:
# rowkey = PERL's test DESCRIPTION (test NUMBERS are the unstable coordinate,
# task #177), with the same fallbacks as perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv: "#N" for
# an unnamed test, "*extra* <desc>" for a PCL-ONLY row, "*summary*" for the
# log's test#-0 summary rows.  The JOIN KEY is (rel, rowkey), compared as a
# MULTISET.  got/expected are NOT here: perl's TAP does not carry them on the
# ok line (they are in the diag, which the runner does not keep).
# the files it MEASURED; a file that produced no comparable TAP this run keeps
# its blessed rows (they are UNVERIFIED, never "fixed").
# THE CAUSE COLUMN (task #993 I3 / docs/plan-test-audit-s464.md, added s473t4):
# an OPTIONAL sixth field naming why the row diverges, in the sweep baseline's
# spelling — a task number (`#1234`), a not-supported anchor (`NS:<section>`),
# a parking note (`PARKED: …`), a catalogue pointer (`CATALOG …`), or a
# combination.  A cause-less row is QUEUE, not baseline, and every run prints
# `CAUSES: N of M blessed row(s) have no cause`.  A row with no cause writes
# FIVE fields, exactly as before, so an unattributed row is byte-identical to
# THE ROWKEY MAY NOT CONTAIN A TAB, and since s473t4 it cannot:
# PclTapAlign::rowkey_desc — the ONE key projection, shared with
# perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv — normalizes it to a space.  Three blessed rows
# carried one (perl runs the `re_tests` HEADER line as a test:
# and run/fresh_perl.t in the other file), and the five-field parse survived
# them only because the key was LAST.  The cause column makes it not-last, so
# those two rows were edited here BY HAND, tabs to spaces, nothing else.
# NOT IN HERE: files registered in perl-suite-expected.tsv (XDIFF) or
# perl-suite-fixture.tsv (FIXTURE) — their rows are already gated per row by
# those registries, and one row must have exactly one gate.
# TRUNCATION: a file with more than 500 diverging rows writes only its first
# 500 to the per-test log, so its multiset here is PARTIAL and a new failure
# past row 500 is invisible.  The log says so in a `# TRUNCATED:` line and the
# runner counts such files in every report.
# *rows-unstable*: a file whose ONLY line here is
# opts OUT of the row check and KEEPS that line through a bless — the same
# hand-placed opt-out perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv has carried since s336.  It
# is a MEASURED claim: the file's row SET is nondeterministic, its COUNTS are
# not, so the count snapshot and the shortfall still gate it.  Registered
# s468be (task #1082): op/hash.t, op/inc.t, op/undef.t, op/utfhash.t, whose
# descriptions interpolate perl's own hash order ("uses >0 heads (6)", "k1:
# delete", "key '2' incremented correctly") and were measured DIFFERENT in two
#   s470bk + s470br (see the notes below) + s470bs-merge 2026-09-06
#   after READING every removed row) -- hand-merged, only the named
#   + s470bx 2026-09-06 (op/stat_errors.t ONLY, 22 rows removed BY HAND --
#   no --bless-fails, so no other file's rows could move).
# s470bx 2026-09-06 -- TWENTY-TWO rows FIXED in op/stat_errors.t, ONE cause:
#   task #1043, `stat`/`lstat` answer their CONTEXT.  The file's assertion is
#   so for the two non-filetest ops it expects perl's &PL_sv_no -- the EMPTY
#   STRING -- where PCL used to hand back the 13-element vector in every
#   context.  All 22 are `result of stat|lstat <arg>` over the eleven operand
#   spellings; the matching `error from ...` rows are untouched (they are
#   #1231's, still failing because an undeclared bareword dies in the
#   compiler).  Verdict op/stat_errors.t P 638/0 C 510/128 -> C 532/106,
#   parallel and serial agreeing (#366 re-run: "REAL MOVE"); measured on a
#   `git archive fcf076f1` extraction as 510/128, which is what makes the
#   mover THIS change and not an inherited one.
#   THEN A HUNDRED AND FOUR MORE, same file, one cause: tasks #1231 + #1044,
#   a BAREWORD in an EXPR handle slot is a handle NAME.  This file's arguments
#   are barewords (NEVEROPENED, SCALARFILE, CLOSEDFILE, CLOSEDDIR, _) reached
#   through `eval "$op $arg"`, and inside a fragment there is no `open` to
#   teach the old file-wide handle registry, so every one compiled to a CALL
#   and DIED inside the eval -- `is $res, undef` passed by accident and
#   `is 0+$err, EBADF` could not, because the die never touched $!.  Verdict
#   532/106 -> 636/2, parallel and serial agreeing.  EXACTLY TWO rows remain,
#   `error from -T \*_` and `error from -B \*_`, a different question (the
#   -T/-B glob-ref-to-`_` operand); they are the two kept here, taken from the
# s470bi (task #1022 half (a), RULED by Fable in s470 and blessed with its
#   cost VISIBLE): a bare `last`/`next`/`redo` whose loop is not lexically in
#   the sub now DIES at its own site, trappably, instead of doing nothing
#   silently (`for` ran to completion: n=303 where perl says 1) or reaching
#   SBCL as "attempt to GO to nonexistent tag".  TWENTY-FIVE rows therefore
#   stop being PRODUCED, in two files, with ONE cause:
#     op/loopctl.t   22 rows -> (missing).  #1022(a): sub test_last { last } dies at the site; rows after it wait on #1022(b)
#       Its `sub test_last { last }` is called at line 920 outside any eval,
#       so the file aborts at test 41 and rows 41-67 never run.
#     op/rt119311.t   3 rows -> (missing).  #1022(a): the six `{ foo(sub { ...; last }) }` sites die at the site; waits on #1022(b)
#       (rows 7-9; 10-18 were already blessed missing, and 19/20's PCL
#   NOT FIXED, WAITING: half (b) -- a catch frame per loop ENTRY -- wins every
#   one of these rows back, and when it lands they must be re-verified, not
#   assumed (a row that fails for a NEW reason is a NEW row).
# s470bk 2026-09-05 -- SEVEN rows FIXED, in two files, with two causes, both
#   shipped by s470bi and merged to main before this bless (the rows are
#   BI's residue: its worktree was gone, so the bookkeeping fell here).
#   Every removed row was READ from this run's .suitelog/*.fails.tsv:
#     op/closure.t  4 rows -> gone.  #1083 (a sub whose body compiles perl at
#       RUN time is cloned per evaluation): *summary*, "cloneable with //ee",
#       "cloneable with use re eval", and "cloning closure proto with no
#       CvOUTSIDE" (that last one was `(missing)`, not `not ok` -- it is the
#       row #1084's do-FILE fix made PRODUCIBLE, which is why the SHORTFALL
#       row for the same file went 1 -> 0 in the same run).
#       Verdict op/closure.t P 281/1 C 277/5, parallel and serial agreeing.
#     op/gv.t       3 rows -> gone.  #1020 (`undef *GLOB` clears every slot,
#       where it used to be a silent no-op): "[at t/op/gv.t line 105]",
#       and serial agreeing; its 4 aborted forms ("Died at gv.t line N") are
#       PRE-EXISTING and already on the snapshot row.
# s470br (task #1115, 2026-09-05): FOURTEEN rows removed BY EDIT -- io/utf8.t
#   (10), uni/gv.t (3), io/bom.t (1) -- and nothing else of those files, whose
#   other rows still diverge.  The io/ ones are #1115: a handle carries OCTETS
#   unless a layer says otherwise, so their byte counts agree with perl now
#   (base 13/14 -> 23/4 and 0/3 -> 1/2, both measured against a `git archive
#   f728637` extraction).  The three uni/gv.t rows -- the `undef *GLOB` slot
#   rows at t/uni/gv.t 110-112 -- are NOT mine: the base tree passes them too,
#   so this baseline was stale for that file before s470br.
# s470bs-merge (2026-09-06, the batch's OWED companion legs): 394 rows REMOVED
#   over TWO files, `--bless-fails` after READING every removed row, and only
#   these six files were measured (op/filetest.t, op/stat.t, op/filetest_t.t,
#   io/fs.t, op/time.t, op/stat_errors.t; the other 263 files' rows are the
#   previous bless, byte-for-byte).  Both causes are s470bs's own, MEASURED
#   against a `git archive 48d8e39` extraction that reproduces the old numbers
#     op/stat_errors.t  205 rows -> gone.  #1033 (perl's ERRNO for the whole
#       family: EBADF for a handle that is not open, ENOENT for a missing
#       path).  Every one of the 205 is an `error from -X <operand>` row.
#       Verdict C 305/333 -> C 510/128, parallel and serial agreeing.
#     op/filetest.t     189 rows -> gone.  #1031 (a filetest runs its operand's
#       the two stacked-`-l` error rows and the two `$ioref` rows) and #1048
#       (the GLOB/IO string-overload rows).  Verdict C 180/254 -> C 369/65,
#       parallel and serial agreeing; its one aborted form ("Undefined
#       subroutine &main::f called") is PRE-EXISTING and unchanged.
#   The remaining 68 + 128 rows are NOT fixed and stay blessed: #1231 (an
#   undeclared bareword in a filetest slot is emitted as a CALL and dies --
#   that is stat_errors.t's whole remaining 128), #1234 (a stacked filetest
#   over a `-X`-overloaded operand re-dispatches at every level; a COMPILER
#   change) and #1235 (`-t`/`-T`/`-B` on an IO ref).
# s470bv 2026-09-06 (Opus, edited ROW BY ROW by a script that uses the runner's
#   OWN key projection, PclTapAlign::rowkey_desc -- NOT --bless-fails, which
#   regenerates the header and would have dropped every note above).  TWENTY-FOUR
#   files re-measured on the s470bv tree (`--jobs 1`, plus the #366 serial re-run:
#   every one "REAL MOVE, both runs agree"); 1962 rows replaced by 1353.  They are
#   the row half of the 51-row perl-suite-run.tsv splice and carry the SAME causes.
#   FOUR files leave entirely because they now MATCH perl: io/perlio.t (26 rows),
#   opbasic/cmp.t (500, the log cap), re/bigfuzzy_not_utf8.t (1), re/reg_60508.t (1).
#   ELEVEN rows are NEW and every one was read and explained before it was written:
#     run/switchC.t 3   "-CI: read in UTF-8 input", "-Ci: auto-UTF-8 open for
#       input", "-Co: auto-UTF-8 open for output".  #1115: they passed only because
#       PCL decoded EVERYTHING by default, i.e. `-C` was permanently on by accident.
#       PCL implements the switch nowhere -- task #1272.
#       not-supported.md "local on hash/array elements and typeglobs",
#       cl/skip-registry.lisp) that used to pass by accident.
#     uni/method.t 2    two of the THIRTEEN rows #1221 made producible at all --
#       the file used to abort before them.  Residual bug: task #1274.
#     op/magic.t 1      ".. and the UTF-8 version is written".  #1221 made
#       `utf8::encode` real, so the row stopped comparing a wide string with
#       itself; `$0 = <wide>` must store the OCTETS -- task #1275.  (The row it
#       traded places with, "ENV store encodes high utf8 in SV", now passes; the
#       file's COUNT is unchanged at 176/31, which is why only the row baseline
#     io/perlio_open.t 1 "open my $fh, '+>>', undef" -- the file used to produce
#       NOTHING (0/0) and now produces 9/1; the row is newly PRODUCED, not newly
#       broken.  Stale before the s470 batches (task #1276).
#     op/rt119311.t 1 + re/charset.t 1: both `*summary*`.  rt119311's baseline row
#       held the RAW summary text where the key projection writes `*summary*` (an
#       older bless); charset's follows its count (2775 -> 2776 not-ok, one more
#   NOT TOUCHED on purpose: io/pvbm.t (the known contention flake), op/utfhash.t
#   (its hand-placed *rows-unstable* opt-out), and every file registered in
# s473 2026-09-06 (Fable, edited ROW BY ROW with :raw handles; NOT re-blessed --
#   `--bless-fails` regenerates the header and drops every note in this file, measured
#   this session and reverted).  SIX files re-measured serially on main d348dcea after
#   the companion --all --quick: their row blocks are replaced by that run's rows
#   (87 FIXED rows leave, 17 NEW rows enter); every other row is byte-identical.
#   run/runenv_randseed.t -1, op/tiearray.t +15: the causes are in
#   s470bs filetest operand resolver) and DECIDED §s473.
# s473t1 (2026-09-07): SIXTEEN rows LEFT BY EDIT -- they PASS.
#   op/multideref.t 13 (exists: general, the six delete:*, the six !exists:*,
#     ONE-argument (p-exists VALUE) because _elem_container_key did not see
#     through the unary `+`, and the raw CL "invalid number of arguments: 1"
#     aborted the file's whole top-level form at test 52.  The 13 rows never
#     RAN; 12 pass now and `delete: const indices` fails on the pre-existing
#     `local`-not-restored rows above it (it stays in the fail baseline).
#     key in a kv-slice was compiled as a SUB CALL.
# s473b 2026-09-07 (task #1241/#1456): ONE row swapped in op/multideref.t, by
#   EDIT, counts unchanged (53/12 before and after, measured --jobs 1 on both
#   trees).  `no strict refs, exist` LEFT this file -- it PASSES now, because
#   an intermediate slot holding a defined STRING is a SYMBOLIC REFERENCE
#   again instead of being CLOBBERED by a fresh hash (#1456 closed).
#   `strict refs, not exist` JOINED it: with the write now landing in
#   %strict_refs::foo as perl does under `no strict`, the row that asserts the
#   key is ABSENT under `use strict refs` fails honestly -- PCL models no
#   strict-refs hint at all (docs/not-supported.md "use strict refs is not
#   enforced").  The same trade appears in baselines/fail-baseline.tsv.
# s484d (2026-09-14, Opus) -- NINE files' row blocks REPLACED by this round's
#   own measurement, every row caused.  The round adds four missing
#   perl-tests/t/test.pl helpers, so these files produce rows they never
#   produced before; each verdict was measured `--jobs 1`, the runner's #366
#   serial re-run AGREES on all nine ("REAL MOVE (both runs agree)"), and the
#   same files were measured first on a `git archive f6b56feb` extraction.
#       NO-OP, so the file reported 1..0; it now produces all 95 of perl's
#       rows, 14 passing.  63 of the 81 failures are `tie` announcing "a HASH
#       (class X) is not implemented" (#155); the residue is #1768.
#     op/fork.t            27 -> 8 rows (19 keys FIXED).  Same cause; 28 rows,
#       `crash:sb-sys:interactive-interrupt` and the file did NOT crash: the
#       text is a CHILD program's diagnostic quoted inside a TAP comment (the
#       record at line 70 does `kill 'INT', $cid`), and the runner's signature
#       scan does not skip comments.  Noted in #1770.
#     op/runlevel.t         1 -> 16 rows.  Same cause; 24 rows, 8 passing.
#       7 of the 16 are #155, the rest loop-control/label diagnostics: #1769.
#     op/anonsub.t         14 -> 8 rows.  Same cause; 15 rows, 6 passing.  The
#       four `'sub;' is illegal` rows are principle 9 (PCL does not reject
#       invalid perl); the three records + `undef &anon` are #1771.
#     io/data.t             1 -> 1 row.  Same cause; 4 rows, 3 passing.  The
#       remaining row is #1767 (`tell(DATA)` is an offset inside the DATA
#       section, perl's is an offset in the file).
#       the file runs to the end: 7/0, DIFF -> **OK**.
#       `not ok N # TODO & SKIP` row is emitted as perl emits it and that row
#       stops diverging.  The other nine keep their blessed attribution
#       (which is none -- they are the audit's queue, untouched here).
#       (#1590) exist, so the file produces all 111 of perl's rows where it
#       produced NONE, 94 passing.  #1772 has the six clusters.
#     run/runenv_hashseed.t 269 -> 4 rows.  Same cause; 278 rows = perl's, 274
#       passing.  The four survivors' cause is corrected #1590 -> **#1588**
#       (PERL_HASH_SEED / PERL_PERTURB_KEYS are inert), which is what they
#       always were once the file could run.
